title: Understand RANK vs DENSE_RANK
learning_objective: Learn why DENSE_RANK is useful when tied salaries should share a rank without gaps.

tutorial.explanation: RANK leaves gaps after ties, while DENSE_RANK does not. Top salary problems usually use DENSE_RANK when tied salaries should all count.
tutorial.syntax: DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS dense_rank
tutorial.mental_model: DENSE_RANK ranks distinct salary values, not individual employees.

guided_example.solution_query: SELECT employee_name, salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS dense_rank FROM employees;
guided_example.explanation: Bob and Cara tie for dense rank 2, and Dan becomes dense rank 3.

practice.prompt: Return employee_name, salary, and dense_rank by salary descending.
practice.expected_query: SELECT employee_name, salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS dense_rank FROM employees;

hints: Put ORDER BY salary DESC inside OVER.
